title: Seamless control-plane rollforward with traffic shadowing and health scrubbing
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Implement an automated, low-risk control-plane rollforward pipeline for Private (VPC) deployments that uses traffic shadowing, progressive promotion, and a battery of health-scrubbing checks so we can ship control-plane versions with minimal user-visible disruption. This ticket covers: 1) Terraform/IaC module changes to express versioned control-plane artifacts and a canary stack; 2) an orchestration pipeline (CI/CD) that performs staged shadowing -> canary -> promote with gating; 3) health probes and automated rollback criteria; and 4) runbooks and dashboards for operators.

Background/context: Customers on Private deployments have strict SLAs and cannot tolerate noisy upgrades. Current ad-hoc upgrade steps require manual coordination and limited telemetry on regressions. We need a repeatable pipeline that: - allows a new control-plane version to be deployed to a subset of private control-planes in a shadowed mode (receive mirrored traffic) - runs synthetic and live health-scrubbing probes that validate API surface compatibility and control-plane operational metrics - promotes cohorts only when scorecards pass, otherwise automatically roll back and quarantine the release.

Design proposal (high level):
- Terraform: introduce a controlplane_version resource and canary_profile module. The module will: create a canary controlplane namespace/cluster variant, attach network routing to accept shadowed TCP/HTTP traffic (no production write path), and register version metadata in the control plane registry (consumed by the orchestration pipeline). Module changes live in repo: terraform/private-controlplane/modules/canary-profile. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8423 (WIP).
- Shadowing: use traffic-mirroring at the ingress layer for compatible API calls (configurable by route). Shadowed requests are allowed to exercise the new control plane without changing customer-facing responses. We will reuse the existing shadowing proxy (proxy-shadower v1.4) and add a small header (X-Shadow-Run) to mark mirrored traffic.
- Health-scrubbing probes: three tiers: 1) API compatibility probes (schema checks, RPC round-trips using golden-prompts); 2) resource integrity checks (operator APIs, CRD validations); 3) operational telemetry checks (CPU/latency error-rate/kv-cache-hit). Each probe returns a pass/fail and a per-probe confidence score. Probe definitions live in: https://confluence.redwood.ai/private/controlplane-upgrades.
- Gating logic: the promotion pipeline computes a rolling score across the canary cohort. Default gate: >= 95% API pass on golden-prompts AND error-rate increase < 0.5% AND P95 latency regression < 15% over baseline. Gates are pluggable and configurable per-release.
- Rollback: automated rollback triggers if any hard threshold breaching occurs (e.g., any intolerable error spill, control-plane panics, or degraded leader-election). Rollbacks must be able to happen within 10 minutes of detection (goal).
- Compatibility matrix and migration adapters: the pipeline must consult a compatibility matrix for model-serving components (KV cache format, session serialization). If the new version introduces incompatible serialized formats, the pipeline should mark the release as requiring a data-migration window and bail out of automated promotion.

Acceptance criteria (must-haves):
- Terraform module merged that can instantiate a canary control-plane variant with a version tag and network routing for shadowing.
- CI/CD orchestration job that performs: deploy -> shadow for 1 hour (configurable) -> run probes -> evaluate gates -> auto-promote cohort-by-cohort OR rollback.
- Health probes implemented and producing metrics to the private-controlplane-upgrades dashboard (Grafana).
- Automatic rollbacks validated in a simulated fault-injection test in staging.
- Operator runbook and upgrade checklist published: https://docs.redwood.ai/operator/runbooks/controlplane-rollforward.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for Terraform modules using terratest harness.
- End-to-end upgrade test in a staging VPC with synthetic workloads that mimic customer token distributions.
- Fault-injection matrix: leader loss, KV cache corruption simulation, slow disk I/O. Validate rollback triggers.

Observability and alerts:
- Dashboards: private-controlplane-upgrades (new panel group). Watch KPIs: API-pass-rate, mirrored-error-rate, p95 latency delta, control-plane restarts, leader-election time.
- Pager thresholds: if mirrored-error-rate > 2% for 5m AND production-error-rate delta > 0.2% escalate to on-call.
- Automated Slack notifications in #infra-upgrades with PR links and cohort promotion events.

Runbook snippets (operator flow):
1) Kick off release job in CI with release tag.
2) Observe 1-hour shadow window; if probes pass, pipeline will promote the first cohort.
3) If promotion pauses, follow guided checklist (capture traces, add debug flags, optionally increase shadow window).
4) If rollback occurs, open postmortem and block further promotions until root cause triage.

Security and compliance notes: shadowed traffic contains customer requests; ensure shadow copies are treated as sensitive (obfuscate PII in mirrored payloads) and are deleted after retention window. KMS policies for canary logs must align with enterprise controls.

Artifacts and links:
- Infra PR (Terraform module): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8423 (WIP)
- Orchestration pipeline prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane-rollouts/pull/19
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/private/controlplane-upgrades
- Staging dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/private-controlplane-upgrades

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Shadowing fidelity vs cost: high-fidelity mirroring increases load and cost for canary infra. We can sample (1:10) to reduce cost but may miss rare regressions.
- Promotion cadence: do we promote by customer cohorts (tenant-based) or by geographic region? Proposal: start with small tenant cohorts, then region-aware cohorts once stable.
- Data migrations: some control-plane changes require coordinated data migrations; automatic pipeline should detect and explicitly block those releases.

Next steps / immediate tasks:
- Finish Terraform module tests (owner: Marcus) and land PR.
- Finalize probe definitions and wire to Grafana (owner: Sreya).
- Add security review checklist and schedule brief with security (owner: Ava).
- Demo run in staging next week with SRE and PM observers.
